title: machine: clean up orphaned gvproxy and win-sshproxy when starting Windows machines
body:
machine: clean up orphaned gvproxy and win-sshproxy when starting Windows machines

Fixes: #29474

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

<!--
Write `None` if there are no user-facing changes, otherwise enter your release note below.
Include "action required" if users need to take action when upgrading.
-->

```release-note
Fixed Windows machine startup failures caused by orphaned gvproxy or win-sshproxy processes left behind by externally stopped wsl VMs.
```
#### PR Description:
- Problem: When a Windows VM is stopped outside Podman, for example with `wsl --shutdown` or `Hyper-V Stop-VM`, `win-sshproxy.exe` or `gvproxy.exe` may remain running on the host and continue to hold the machine's named pipe.
- Fix: Before startup, the state file is read and the actual server PID of the named pipe is retrieved through the Windows API. The old proxy is terminated only when the two PIDs match, which avoids killing an unrelated process. If the PIDs do not match, an error is returned and startup is stopped.
- Tests: Added 2 test cases in the `machine_windows_test.go`: Cleanup is performed when the PID matches; Cleanup is refused when the PID does not match.

comments.body:
> Looks good. I have added a couple of non-blocking comments. I still want to test it before approval. I will do that later.
> 
> @Xiaowen-Yang it would be helpful if you could mention if and how you have tested your changes.

Thanks for reviewing. For testing, I could only test the WSL locally. Therefore, the Hyper-V path remains untested : ).

I built `before.exe` before the modification and `after.exe` after the modification separately in a Windows 11 WSL environment. Using the same Podman machine, I first started it normally and recorded the PID of `win-sshproxy.exe`. Then ran `wsl.exe --terminate <machine-name>` to simulate the VM being terminated unexpectedly by an external action.

When restarting the machine with `before.exe machine start`, the VM started successfully, but Podman reported `could not start api proxy since expected pipe is not available`. The PID of the old `win-sshproxy` process also remained unchanged.

After recreating the same conditions, I started the machine with `after.exe machine start`. The VM started normally without any API forwarding errors, and `API forwarding listening on...` was displayed. The old proxy process was cleaned up, the PID of `win-sshproxy` changed, and the Docker API was also accessible normally.

@Xiaowen-Yang it's failing for me on Hyper-V. The call to `DialPipeContext` times out:

```pwsh
[ADMIN]:PS C:\Users\mario\git\podman> podman machine start
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
Error: could not recover api proxy for podman-machine-default: connecting to named pipe "podman-machine-default": context deadline exceeded
```

And if I manually kill gvproxy and try to restart the machine I get this error:

```pwsh
[ADMIN]:PS C:\Users\mario\git\podman> podman machine start
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
Error: Job failed with error code: 32773. Description: Failed to set value of the 'ignition.config.0' Data Exchange integration service item for virtual machine 'podman-machine-default': The parameter is incorrect. (0x80070057) (Virtual machine ID A077F3C0-004A-0000-0000-000000000000)
```

> An alternative could be to open the pipe handle using windows.CreateFile with FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES access only. This retrieves the handle without triggering gvproxy's connection-accept loop.

Yes. And we can also avoid looking for the owner of the named pipe (the function `namedPipeServerPID`):
- if both the namedPipe and the pid/tid file exists we can safely kill the process
- if only the namedPipe exists but not the pid/tid file we should fail

> > An alternative could be to open the pipe handle using windows.CreateFile with FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES access only. This retrieves the handle without triggering gvproxy's connection-accept loop.

That makes sense, thank you. I simplified the code accordingly, and the WSL test passed. Could you please take another look and, if possible, retest it on Hyper-V? : )
